title: Pokyo Daily – Shore Tragedy
content:
Summer 12, Coral Island

By Maren Castillo, Pokyo Daily Staff Writer

A body was discovered along the shoreline of Coral Island earlier this week. The victim has been identified as the son of a visiting couple. Believing the spot to be his final resting place, the family held a funeral and chose to bury him near the beach.

title: Pokyo Daily – Flowers at the Beach Tomb
content:
Fall 3, Coral Island
By Tomas Wira, Pokyo Daily Correspondent

Years after the tragic drowning of their son, the grieving parents continue to return to Coral Island. The couple is often seen leaving flowers at the beachside tomb where their child was laid to rest. Locals say the visits are welcome, expressing sympathy and solidarity with the family’s enduring loss.

title: Island Regulation 14.3
content:
Regulation 14.3 — Maximum number of goats allowed in a canoe: 2.

This ordinance was passed after multiple incidents of capsized boats at sea. Local farmers were attempting to transport herds by water, resulting in damage to property and, in one case, a goat being rescued from the lighthouse pier.

To ensure the safety of both livestock and passengers, all watercraft must comply with this limit. Anyone caught exceeding the number will be fined one basket of fresh produce and ordered to attend a mandatory ‘Safe Boating with Goats’ workshop.
